name: Chandigarh
description: The City Beautiful, planned by Le Corbusier, featuring the UNESCO World Heritage Capitol Complex, Nek Chand Rock Garden, and Sukhna Lake.

name: Delhi
description: National Capital Territory of India featuring three UNESCO World Heritage monuments (Qutub Minar, Humayun's Tomb, Red Fort), India Gate, and Chandni Chowk.

name: Faridabad
description: Historic industrial city home to 10th-century Surajkund sun pool stepwell amphitheatre, annual International Crafts Mela, and Raja Nahar Singh Palace.

name: Gurugram
description: Millennium City combining futuristic cyber hubs with heritage Sheesh Mahal at Farrukhnagar, Sultanpur Bird Sanctuary, and Sheetla Mata temple.

name: Hisar
description: Historical fortified city founded in 1354 by Firoz Shah Tughlaq featuring Firoz Shah Palace complex, Lat Ki Masjid, and Harappan Rakhigarhi.

name: Kurukshetra
description: Sacred cradle of the Bhagavad Gita, huge Brahma Sarovar holy tank, Jyotisar banyan tree enlightenment site, and Sheikh Chilli tomb.

name: Panipat
description: City of Weavers and legendary battleground of three epoch-defining Indian wars, holding Kabuli Bagh Mosque, Ibrahim Lodi Tomb, and Hemu memorial.

name: Yamunanagar
description: Foothill district featuring Kalesar National Park sal forests, Buddhist stupa at Chaneti, and ancient Sugh archaeological mound.

name: Bilaspur
description: Picturesque valley city on the emerald Gobind Sagar reservoir formed by Bhakra Dam, water sports hub, and Vyas Cave.

name: Chamba
description: Ancient Ravi river kingdom famed for 10th-century stone Lakshmi Narayan temples, Chaugan green, Chamba Rumal embroidery, and Rang Mahal.

name: Dalhousie

name: Dharamshala
description: Seat of the 14th Dalai Lama in Upper McLeod Ganj, Tsuglagkhang Buddhist temple, pine-shaded mountain trails, and scenic HPCA cricket stadium.

name: Kangra
description: Historic town home to the impregnable 4th-century BCE Kangra Fort (oldest dated fort in Himalayas) and Brajeshwari Devi Shakti Peetha.

name: Kasauli
description: Peaceful British-era cantonment hill station framed by oak and cedar woods, Christ Church, Gilbert Nature Trail, and Monkey Point.

name: Keylong
description: Administrative center of Lahaul valley situated above the Bhaga river, home to Shashur and Kardang Buddhist monasteries.

name: Kullu
description: Valley of the Gods renowned for the International Dussehra festival on Dhalpur ground, Raghunath Temple, and Kullu handloom shawls.

name: Manali
description: High-altitude resort town at the northern end of Kullu Valley, featuring 1553 timber Hidimba Devi temple, Solang Valley, and Atal Tunnel gateway.

name: Paonta Sahib
description: Sacred Yamuna riverbank town where Guru Gobind Singh penned the Dasam Granth, housing Gurdwara Paonta Sahib and historic museum.

name: Shimla
description: Former British summer capital, UNESCO Kalka-Shimla Toy Train terminal, pedestrian Mall Road, neo-Gothic Christ Church, and Viceregal Lodge.

name: Spiti Valley
description: The Middle Land trans-Himalayan desert holding 1000-year-old Key Monastery, Tabo UNESCO tentative monastery, and high fossil village Langza.

name: Reckong Peo
description: Headquarters of Kinnaur offering spellbinding views of the sacred Kinnaur Kailash peak, apple orchards, and Kalpa heritage village.

name: Anantnag
description: Commercial capital of South Kashmir known for mineral water springs, 8th-century Martand Sun Temple ruins, and gateway to Amarnath Cave.

name: Gulmarg
description: Meadow of Flowers, premier winter ski resort of India, holding the world's second-highest operating cable car (Gulmarg Gondola to Apharwat peak at 13,780 ft).

name: Jammu
description: City of Temples and winter capital on the Tawi River, holding historic Bahu Fort, Raghunath Temple, Amar Mahal palace museum, and gateway to Vaishno Devi.

name: Pahalgam
description: Valley of the Shepherds on the Lidder River, starting point for the annual Amarnath Yatra, featuring Betaab Valley, Aru Valley, and Baisaran meadow.

name: Patnitop
description: Picturesque pine-forested plateau at 6,640 ft along the Jammu-Srinagar highway, Skyview cable car ropeway, Sanasar Lake, and Nag Temple.

name: Srinagar
description: Summer capital situated in the heart of Kashmir Valley, world-famous for Dal Lake houseboats and shikaras, Mughal Pleasure Gardens, and wooden Jama Masjid.

name: Kargil
description: Historic transit city on the Suru river, holding the Kargil War Memorial at Dras, ancient Rock-cut Maitreya Buddha at Mulbekh, and gateway to Zanskar.

name: Leh
description: Capital of Ladakh at 11,500 ft, featuring the 9-storey 17th-century Leh Palace, white Shanti Stupa, Hemis & Thiksey monasteries, and Khardung La pass.

name: Amritsar
description: Spiritual and cultural capital of Sikhism holding the gold-gilded Sri Harmandir Sahib (Golden Temple), Jallianwala Bagh national memorial, and Wagah Border.

name: Fatehgarh Sahib
description: Hallowed Sikh pilgrimage town marking the martyrdom site of Sahibzada Zorawar Singh and Fateh Singh, holding Gurdwara Fatehgarh Sahib.

name: Fazilka
description: Border heritage town known as Bangla on the Sutlej, historic Asafwala War Memorial, Sadiqi border retreat ceremony, and Toshi footwear.

name: Firozepur
description: Historic border fortress city along the Sutlej holding the National Martyrs Memorial at Hussainiwala (Bhagat Singh, Rajguru, Sukhdev) and Saragarhi memorial.

name: Gurdaspur
description: Majha heritage district holding Dera Baba Nanak (gateway to Kartarpur Corridor), historic Takht-e-Akbari coronation platform of Akbar at Kalanaur.

name: Jalandhar
description: Ancient Doaba city mentioned in Mahabharata, sports goods manufacturing capital of India, Devi Talab Mandir, and Wonderland theme park.

name: Kapurthala
description: Paris of Punjab celebrated for Indo-French architecture in Jagatjit Palace (modeled on Versailles), Moorish Mosque, Elysee Palace, and Shalimar Gardens.

name: Ludhiana
description: Manchester of India on the Sutlej river featuring Maharaja Ranjit Singh War Museum, historic Lodhi Fort, and Punjab Agricultural University.

name: Pathankot
description: Strategic gateway city where Punjab, J&K and Himachal meet, home to 9th-century Shahpurkandi Fort on the Ravi, Nurpur Fort, and Mukteshwar temple caves.

name: Patiala
description: Royal heritage city famed for the colossal Sikh-Mughal Qila Mubarak fort complex, Sheesh Mahal mirror palace, Baradari Gardens, and Patiala Shahi turban.

name: Rupnagar
description: Historic Ropar holding prominent Harappan Indus Valley Civilization archaeological excavated mound and museum, wetland sanctuary, and canals.

name: SAS Nagar
description: Mohali — modern commercial and sports metropolis holding Fateh Burj (tallest minar in India celebrating victory of Baba Banda Singh Bahadur) and PCA Stadium.

name: Ajmer
description: Spiritual oasis in the Aravalli hills holding the world-renowned Sufi shrine Dargah Sharif of Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti, Adhai Din Ka Jhonpra, and Taragarh Fort.

name: Alwar
description: Gateway city of Rajasthan crowned by Bala Quila fort, marble Moosi Maharani ki Chhatri, City Palace, and gateway to Sariska Tiger Reserve and Bhangarh.

name: Banswara
description: City of Hundred Islands set amidst the Mahi river archipelago, green southern Aravalli hills, Anand Sagar Lake, and Arthuna medieval temple ruins.

name: Bharatpur
description: Eastern gateway of Rajasthan famed for Keoladeo National Park (UNESCO bird paradise), Lohagarh Fort (iron fort that withstood British sieges), and Deeg Water Palaces.

name: Bikaner
description: Desert citadel featuring the invincible red sandstone Junagarh Fort, Lalgarh Palace, Karni Mata rat temple at Deshnoke, and camel breeding center.

name: Bundi
description: Untouched Rajput town celebrated for the dramatic cliff-hugging Taragarh Fort, frescoed Bundi murals in Chitrashala, and 50+ ornate stepwells like Raniji ki Baori.

name: Chittorgarh
description: Symbol of Rajput chivalry, largest fort in India (UNESCO), holding Vijay Stambha (Tower of Victory), Kirti Stambha, and Queen Padmini's Palace.

name: Dausa
description: Historic district home to the architectural wonder Chand Baori stepwell at Abhaneri (3,500 geometric steps), Harshat Mata temple, and Mehandipur Balaji.

name: Dholpur
description: Red sandstone city on the Chambal river holding the historic Machkund sacred water tank, Shergarh Fort, royal chhatris, and National Chambal Sanctuary.

name: Jaipur
description: The Pink City (UNESCO World Heritage), holding the honeycombed Hawa Mahal, Amer Fort hill complex, City Palace, and Jantar Mantar astronomical observatory.

name: Jaisalmer
description: The Golden City rising out of the Thar Desert, holding the living Sonar Qila (UNESCO Golden Fort), Patwon ki Haveli, Gadisar Lake, and Sam sand dunes.

name: Jodhpur
description: The Blue City crowned by the colossal Mehrangarh Fort rising 400 feet above the city, Umaid Bhawan Art Deco palace, and marble Jaswant Thada memorial.

name: Kota
description: Industrial and educational hub on the Chambal river, holding the Garh City Palace with Rajput miniature frescoes, Kishore Sagar Jagmandir, and Seven Wonders Park.

name: Mount Abu
description: Only hill station in Rajasthan at 4,000 ft in the Aravallis, home to the exquisite 11th-13th century Dilwara Jain marble temples, Nakki Lake, and Guru Shikhar peak.

name: Udaipur
description: City of Lakes and Venice of the East, holding the sprawling City Palace complex on Lake Pichola, island Lake Palace (Taj), Jag Mandir, and Saheliyon-ki-Bari.

name: Agra
description: Mughal imperial capital holding the iconic white marble Taj Mahal (UNESCO), Agra Fort, Itmad-ud-Daulah (Baby Taj), and nearby Fatehpur Sikri (UNESCO).

name: Ayodhya
description: Sacred birthplace of Lord Rama on the holy Saryu river, holding the grand Ram Mandir, Hanuman Garhi fortress temple, and ancient Ram Ki Paidi ghats.

name: Bareilly
description: Historic Rohilkhand trade city celebrated for Zari-Zardozi embroidery, cane furniture, seven ancient Shiva Nath temples (Alakhnath, Trivatinath), and Jhumka.

name: Chitrakoot
description: Sacred pilgrim town straddling the Mandakini river, holding Bharat Milap shrine, Hanuman Dhara spring temple on a cliff, and Sphatik Shila rock footprints.

name: Jhansi
description: Gateway to Bundelkhand and seat of legendary 1857 warrior queen Rani Lakshmibai, holding the formidable granite Jhansi Fort and Government Museum.

name: Kanpur
description: Major industrial and historical city on the Ganges holding 5th-century Gupta brick temple at Bhitargaon, Bithoor sacred ghats of Maharishi Valmiki, and Allen Forest Zoo.

name: Lucknow
description: City of Nawabs famed for refined Tehzeeb culture, colossal gravity-defying arch of Bara Imambara (Bhulbhulaiya maze), Rumi Darwaza, and Chikankari embroidery.

name: Mathura
description: Sacred birthplace of Lord Krishna on the Yamuna river, holding Shri Krishna Janmasthan temple, Vishram Ghat aarti, and neighboring sacred Vrindavan.

name: Prayagraj
description: Triveni Sangam sacred confluence of Ganga, Yamuna, and mythical Saraswati, site of the Maha Kumbh Mela, Mughal Allahabad Fort, and Anand Bhavan.

name: Varanasi
description: Spiritual capital of India and one of the world's oldest living cities, featuring sacred Ganga river ghats, Kashi Vishwanath Jyotirlinga, and nearby Sarnath (UNESCO).

name: Almora
description: Cultural capital of Kumaon perched on a horse-saddle ridge, holding Bright End Corner sunset point, Kasar Devi hippie trail, and Jageshwar temple valley.

name: Badrinath
description: Premier Himalayan Char Dham holy shrine of Lord Vishnu on the Alaknanda River, framed by Nar and Narayana mountain ranges, Tapt Kund, and Mana village.

name: Berinag
description: Tranquil Kumaon town renowned for tea gardens, serpent temples (Nag Devta), and panoramic vistas of the snow-clad Panchachuli and Nanda Devi peaks.

name: Bhimtal
description: Scenic lake resort town centered on a picturesque lake with an island aquarium, Victorian dam, and 17th-century Bhimeshwar Mahadev temple.

name: Chamoli
description: Himalayan district gateway to UNESCO Valley of Flowers, Hemkund Sahib high-altitude lake, Badrinath, and cradle of the historic Chipko forest movement.

name: Dehradun
description: State capital nestled in the Doon Valley, home to Forest Research Institute Greco-Roman architecture, Robber's Cave (Guchhupani), and Mindrolling Monastery.

name: Gangotri
description: Sacred Char Dham high-altitude shrine of Goddess Ganga on the Bhagirathi river at 10,200 ft, gateway to Gaumukh glacier and Tapovan trekking routes.

name: Haridwar
description: Gateway to the Gods where the Ganges leaves the Himalayas, famed for Har Ki Pauri ghat evening Ganga Aarti, Mansa Devi ropeway, and Kumbh Mela.

name: Kausani
description: Switzerland of India as called by Mahatma Gandhi, offering an uninterrupted 300-km panoramic view of Himalayan peaks (Trisul, Nanda Devi, Panchachuli).

name: Kedarnath
description: Most revered Himalayan Jyotirlinga shrine dedicated to Lord Shiva, resting at 11,755 ft near Mandakini river headwaters against the Kedarnath glacier peak.

name: Lansdowne
description: Quiet cantonment hill station founded in 1887, headquarters of the Garhwal Rifles, surrounded by thick oak and blue pine woods, Bhulla Lake, and Tip-in-Top.

name: Mussoorie
description: Queen of the Hills at 6,500 ft, featuring Mall Road promenade, Kempty Falls, Gun Hill cable car, Lal Tibba viewpoint, and colonial heritage estates.

name: Nainital
description: Famous lake district town nestled around the emerald eye-shaped Naini Lake, Naina Devi temple, Snow View cable car, and British Governor's Raj Bhavan.

name: New Tehri
description: Planned modern hill town overlooking Tehri Dam (tallest dam in India) and massive green reservoir lake offering water sports, boating, and scenic vistas.

name: Pithoragarh
description: Little Kashmir in the Soar Valley, border district gateway to Kailash Mansarovar pilgrimage route, Chand-era Pithoragarh Fort, and alpine meadows.

name: Rishikesh
description: Yoga Capital of the World along the turquoise Ganges, famed for Lakshman Jhula, Ram Jhula, Beatles Ashram (Chaurasi Kutia), and whitewater rafting.

name: Uttarkashi
description: Northern holy town on the Bhagirathi river, home to ancient Vishwanath Temple with brass trident, Nehru Institute of Mountaineering, and Gangotri base.

name: Bomdila
description: Picturesque hill town with panoramic vistas of snow-capped Gorichen and Kangto peaks, Buddhist gompas, and apple orchards.

name: Changlang
description: Eastern frontier district gateway to Namdapha National Park, historic World War II Stillwell Road, and Tangsa tribal culture.

name: Dirang
description: Serene mountain valley featuring 500-year-old stone fortified Dirang Dzong, natural hot water springs, and kiwi orchards.

name: Itanagar
description: State capital guarded by the 14th-century irregular brick Ita Fort, serene Ganga Lake (Gyakar Sinyi), and Jawaharlal Nehru State Museum.

name: Mechuka
description: Pristine high-altitude valley bordered by snow peaks, 400-year-old Samten Yongcha gompa, Yargyapchu river, and Memba tribal villages.

name: Namsai
description: Spiritual haven famed for the glittering Burmese-style Golden Pagoda (Kongmu Kham) at Tengapani and Tai Khamti Buddhist festivals.

name: Pakke Kesang Hill Station
description: Untouched emerald hill station known for cool mountain climate, panoramic Himalayan viewpoints, and proximity to Pakke Tiger Reserve.

name: Pasighat
description: Historic British-era settlement nestled where the roaring Siang river meets the plains, gateway to whitewater rafting expeditions.

name: Roing
description: Fascinating valley holding ancient 8th-century burnt-brick fortress of Bhismaknagar, pristine Mehao high-altitude lake, and Idu Mishmi culture.

name: Tawang
description: High-altitude mountain sanctum home to India's largest Buddhist monastery (Tawang Gompa), Sela Pass, and Madhuri Lake.

name: Yingkiong
description: Picturesque hill town set amidst dramatic gorges of the Siang River, traditional bamboo-cane suspension bridges, and Adi tribal villages.

name: Ziro
description: UNESCO-tentative valley renowned for unique sustainable paddy-cum-fish agro-systems, sacred Tarin groves, and annual outdoor Ziro Music Festival.

name: Chirang
description: Bodoland territorial district bordering Bhutan, gateway to Manas National Park UNESCO biodiversity hotspot and Bodo tribal handlooms.

name: Dibrugarh
description: Tea City of India nestled on the Brahmaputra, gateway to lush colonial tea estates, river cruises, and Dehing Patkai rainforest.

name: Guwahati
description: Gateway to Northeast India, home to the sacred Kamakhya Shakti Peetha, Umananda peacock river island, and Brahmaputra ropeway.

name: Jorhat
description: Historical cultural center, home to Tocklai Tea Research Institute, sprawling tea bungalows, and main ferry launch point for Majuli.

name: Majuli
description: World's largest inhabited river island, spiritual heart of Neo-Vaishnavite Satras, traditional bamboo mask-making, and pottery.

name: Sivasagar
description: Imperial capital of the 600-year Ahom Dynasty, famed for Rang Ghar amphitheatre, multi-storied Talatal Ghar palace, and massive tanks.

name: Tezpur
description: City of Eternal Romance along the northern Brahmaputra bank, featuring Agnigarh hill romantic ruins and 6th-century stone doorframe of Da Parbatia.

name: Tinsukia
description: Commercial hub bordering Dibru-Saikhowa National Park, famed for feral horses, Dibru river boat safaris, and Digboi historic oil town.

name: Umrangso
description: Scenic hill town in Dima Hasao district with rolling green hillocks, turquoise Kopili reservoir lakes, and annual Falcon festival.

name: Imphal
description: Capital city holding ancient Kangla Fort, Ima Keithel (world's only women-run market), Shri Govindaji Temple, and gateway to Loktak Lake.

name: Cherrapunjee
description: Sohra — wettest place on Earth featuring dramatic Nohkalikai waterfall, Mawsmai limestone cave, and bio-engineered double-decker living root bridges.

name: Shillong
description: Scotland of the East, pine-covered hill capital featuring Ward's Lake, Elephant Falls, Don Bosco Museum of Indigenous Cultures, and Shillong Peak.

name: Aizawl
description: Spectacular ridge-top capital at 3,700 feet, featuring Solomon's Temple, Mizoram State Museum, Durtlang Hills, and vibrant Bara Bazar handloom market.

name: Champhai
description: Rice Bowl of Mizoram on the Myanmar border with verdant valley views, ancient monoliths at Mungmang, and heart-shaped Rih Dil lake nearby.

name: Lunglei
description: Second largest city of Mizoram named after a stone bridge landmark on the Nghasih stream, offering views of Tlawng river valley and Khawnglung wildlife.

name: Serchhip
description: Central district featuring highest literacy, spectacular Vantawng Falls (highest waterfall in Mizoram), and tranquil Thenzawl handloom village.

name: Dimapur
description: Commercial gateway of Nagaland holding ancient 10th-century Kachari Kingdom mushroom-domed monolith ruins, Diezephe craft village, and Triple Falls.

name: Kohima
description: Hilltop capital holding historic World War II Kohima War Cemetery (Battle of the Tennis Court), Kisama Heritage Village (Hornbill Festival), and Dzukou Valley.

name: Mokokchung
description: Cultural and intellectual heart of the Ao Naga tribe, scenic hill ridges, Longkhum eagle-view village, and traditional Moatsu festival.

name: Gangtok
description: Scenic mountain capital perched at 5,400 ft overlooking Mt. Khangchendzonga, featuring Enchey Monastery, Namgyal Institute of Tibetology, and MG Marg.

name: Mangan
description: Cardamom capital and gateway to high-altitude North Sikkim, alpine Yumthang Valley of Flowers, Gurudongmar glacial lake, and hot springs.

name: Pelling
description: Hill retreat offering closest views of Khangchendzonga, holding 1705 Pemayangtse Monastery, Rabdentse royal ruins, and Singshore suspension bridge.

name: Agartala
description: Royal capital city holding neoclassical white marble Ujjayanta Palace, water palace Neermahal on Rudrasagar Lake, and Tripura Sundari Shakti Peetha.

name: Unakoti
description: Ancient Shaivite pilgrimage wonder in forested hills holding massive 7th-9th century rock-carved reliefs (including 30-foot Shiva Unakotiswara Kal Bhairava).

name: Mayabunder
description: Administrative town in Middle Andaman known for Karmatang beach turtle nesting ground, mangrove creeks, and Karen Burmese settler culture.

name: Rangat
description: Eco-tourism destination in Middle Andaman boasting the Dhaninallah Mangrove Walkway (longest in India), Amkunj beach, and Cutbert Bay turtle haven.

name: Sri Vijaya Puram
description: Territory capital (formerly Port Blair) holding the National Memorial Cellular Jail, Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose Island (Ross Island), and coral beaches.

name: Arrah
description: Historic town famed for 1857 Indian Uprising hero Veer Kunwar Singh fort, Jagdishpur heritage, and Arrah House colonial battleground.

name: Gaya
description: Ancient spiritual sanctum including the Vishnupad Temple on the Falgu river and UNESCO World Heritage Mahabodhi Temple at Bodh Gaya.

name: Nalanda
description: UNESCO World Heritage 5th-century Buddhist university archaeological ruins, multimedia museum, and neighboring Magadha capital Rajgir.

name: Patna
description: Ancient Mauryan capital Pataliputra, home to Takht Sri Patna Sahib, historic Golghar beehive granary, and world-class Bihar Museum.

name: Deoghar
description: Abode of the Gods, home to Baba Baidyanath Jyotirlinga temple complex drawing millions of Kanwariya pilgrims, Naulakha temple, and Trikut Pahar.

name: Jamshedpur
description: The Steel City founded by Jamsetji Tata, an impeccably planned green oasis with Jubilee Park, Dalma Wildlife Sanctuary, and Dimna Lake.

name: Ranchi
description: City of Waterfalls (Hundru, Jonha, Dassam), Pahari Mandir hilltop, Tagore Hill cultural retreat, and tribal heritage museums.

name: Bhubaneswar
description: Temple City of India boasting 500+ sandstone Kalinga temples (Lingaraj, Mukteshvara, Rajarani), 1st-century BCE Udayagiri & Khandagiri Jain caves, and Dhauli.

name: Cuttack
description: Millennium City on the Mahanadi-Kathajodi delta, famed for the medieval 14th-century Barabati Fort, silver filigree Tarakasi crafts, and Bali Yatra.

name: Koraput
description: Eastern Ghats tribal heartland famed for Jagannath Sabara Srikhetra temple, Duduma waterfall, Gupteswar limestone cave, and coffee plantations.

name: Mayurbhanj
description: Royal district home to UNESCO Similipal Biosphere Reserve (tigers and waterfalls), Baripada royal palace, and acrobatic Mayurbhanj Chhau martial dance.

name: Puri
description: Sacred coastal Char Dham holy city centered on the 12th-century Jagannath Temple (Rath Yatra), Golden Beach (Blue Flag), and nearby Konark Sun Temple (UNESCO).

name: Darjeeling
description: Queen of the Hills holding the UNESCO World Heritage Darjeeling Himalayan Railway (Toy Train), Tiger Hill sunrise over Kanchenjunga, and tea gardens.

name: Durgapur
description: Steel city on the Damodar River, planned by Joseph Allen Stein, featuring Durgapur Barrage, Troika Park, and gateway to terracotta temples of Bishnupur.

name: Howrah
description: Historic twin city to Kolkata on the Hooghly river, holding iconic cantilevered Howrah Bridge, Belur Math (Ramakrishna Mission), and Indian Botanical Garden (Great Banyan).

name: Kalimpong
description: Quiet mountain ridge town in the eastern Himalayas renowned for Tibetan Buddhist monasteries (Zang Dhok Palri Phodang), flower nurseries, and Deolo Hill.

name: Kolkata
description: City of Joy and cultural capital of India, featuring Victoria Memorial, Dakshineswar Kali Temple, Indian Museum, Park Street, and Durga Puja festival (UNESCO).

name: Siliguri
description: Strategic transportation hub in the chicken's neck corridor, gateway to Darjeeling, Sikkim, and Bhutan, featuring Salugara Buddhist Stupa and Mahananda sanctuary.

name: Bilaspur
description: Cultural and railway hub featuring the 11th-century Ratanpur Mahamaya Temple, Malhar archaeological remains, and Achanakmar Tiger Reserve.

name: Dantewada
description: Ancient sacred realm situated at the confluence of Shankhini and Dhankini rivers, celebrated for the 14th-century Danteshwari Shakti Peetha.

name: Jagdalpur
description: Tourism capital of Bastar featuring the Niagara of India Chitrakote Falls, Tirathgarh cascades, Kotumsar dripstone caves, and Bastar crafts.

name: Raipur
description: State capital on the Mahanadi basin featuring Purkhouti Muktangan cultural park, Swami Vivekananda Sarovar, and gateway to Sirpur.

name: Rajnandgaon
description: Historic princely seat known for Dongargarh Bambleshwari hilltop temple reached by ropeway, royal palaces, and peace-pagoda monuments.

name: Anuppur
description: Gateway to sacred Amarkantak, the origin of holy Narmada and Son rivers, Narmada Kund temples, and Kapildhara waterfall.

name: Bhopal
description: City of Lakes combining Begum architectural monuments (Taj-ul-Masajid, Shaukat Mahal), Bharat Bhavan arts center, and Upper Lake.

name: Chanderi
description: Medieval Bundelkhand town dominated by a hilltop fort, Badal Mahal Gate, Koshak Mahal, and world-famous sheer Chanderi silk weaving.

name: Chitrakoot
description: Sacred tranquil forest town where Lord Rama spent 11 years of exile, featuring Ramghat on Mandakini river, Kamadgiri, and Gupt Godavari caves.

name: Datia
description: Ancient town boasting the 7-storey stone Bir Singh Palace (marvel of Rajput-Mughal architecture built without wood or iron) and Pitambara Peeth.

name: Gwalior
description: Historic citadel city crowned by the impregnable Gwalior Fort (Pearl in the necklace of forts), Man Singh Palace tiles, and Scindia Jai Vilas Palace.

name: Indore
description: India's cleanest city and Holkar royal capital holding 7-storey Rajwada Palace, glass temple Kanch Mandir, and Sarafa night street-food bazaar.

name: Jabalpur
description: Cultural center on the Narmada featuring dramatic Marble Rocks canyon at Bhedaghat, roaring Dhuandhar waterfall, and Madan Mahal fort.

name: Khajuraho
description: UNESCO World Heritage complex of medieval Hindu and Jain temples renowned for nagara architectural beauty and exquisite sculptural art.

name: Mandsaur
description: Historic Malwa city on the Shivna river famed for the unique eight-faced Pashupatinath Temple and 6th-century Yasodharman victory pillars.

name: Morena
description: Chambal district holding the 64-yogini circular Chausath Yogini Temple at Mitawali (inspiration for Parliament House) and Bateshwar temple complex.

name: Orchha
description: Medieval Bundela kingdom on the boulder-strewn Betwa river featuring Jahangir Mahal palace, Ram Raja Temple (where Rama is king), and chhatris.

name: Pachmarhi
description: Queen of Satpura, only hill station in MP, featuring Pandava Caves, Bee Falls, Dhoopgarh sunset peak (highest in MP), and sal forests.

name: Sanchi
description: UNESCO World Heritage site holding the 3rd-century BCE Great Stupa commissioned by Emperor Ashoka with four exquisitely carved stone torana gates.

name: Ujjain
description: Ancient holy city on the Shipra River, hosting Simhastha Kumbh Mela, Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga temple, and Jantar Mantar observatory.

name: Daman
description: Coastal Portuguese enclave on the Gulf of Khambhat featuring the 16th-century Moti Daman Fort, Church of Bom Jesus, and Devka beach.

name: Diu
description: Picturesque island citadel surrounded by sea waves, holding formidable sea-facing Diu Fort, St. Paul Church, Naida Caves, and Nagoa beach.

name: Silvassa
description: Capital of Dadra and Nagar Haveli, featuring Portuguese Church of Our Lady of Piety, Warli tribal cultural museum, and Madhuban dam reservoir.

name: Goa
description: Coastal paradise famed for UNESCO Churches of Old Goa, Baroque basilicas, Latin Quarters of Fontainhas, coastal forts, and sandy beaches.

name: Ahmedabad
description: India's first UNESCO World Heritage City, home to Sabarmati Ashram, Sidi Saiyyed Mosque filigree stone latticework, and Adalaj Stepwell.

name: Balasinor
description: India's Jurassic Park, site of Raiyoli Dinosaur Fossil Park containing world's largest dinosaur egg hatchery and royal palace heritage.

name: Bhavnagar
description: Historic maritime kingdom with Nilambag Palace, Takhteshwar Temple hill, and gateway to the 800+ marble Jain temples of Palitana.

name: Bhuj
description: Historic desert capital featuring Aina Mahal hall of mirrors, Prag Mahal Venetian gothic palace, and gateway to White Rann artisan villages.

name: Champaner
description: UNESCO World Heritage archaeological park combining pre-Mughal Islamic architecture, stepwells, mosques, and Kalika Mata hilltop shrine.

name: Dwarka
description: Sacred Char Dham coastal pilgrimage center on the Arabian Sea, home to the multi-tiered 72-pillar Dwarkadhish temple of Lord Krishna.

name: Gandhinagar
description: Green capital city planned on the Sabarmati river, home to the colossal carved sandstone Akshardham temple complex and Dandi Kutir museum.

name: Gir Somnath
description: First of the twelve holy Jyotirlinga shrines facing the Arabian Sea, alongside the dry-deciduous forest kingdom of the Asiatic Lions in Gir.

name: Jamnagar
description: Jewel of Kathiawar famed for Lakhota Palace inside a lake, Khijadiya Bird Sanctuary, Marine National Park coral reefs, and Bandhani silk.

name: Junagadh
description: Ancient city at the base of holy Girnar mountain with 3rd-century BCE Ashokan rock edicts, Uparkot Fort, and gothic Mahabat Maqbara.

name: Kutch
description: Vast salt marsh wilderness hosting the world-famous Rann Utsav, Dholavira UNESCO Harappan archaeological site, and vibrant Rogan embroidery.

name: Patan
description: Medieval Solanki capital housing UNESCO World Heritage Rani ki Vav seven-storey subterranean stepwell and master Patola silk weavers.

name: Porbandar
description: Ancient port and birthplace of Mahatma Gandhi (Kirti Mandir memorial), Sudama Temple, flamingo-filled wetlands, and coastal promenades.

name: Rajkot
description: Heart of Saurashtra with Kaba Gandhi No Delo childhood home of Mahatma Gandhi, Watson Museum, and renowned silver jewelry craft.

name: Surat
description: Diamond City and historic Mughal trading port on the Tapi river, famous for textile markets, Dutch and British colonial cemeteries, and food.

name: Vadnagar
description: Continuous 2,500-year-old archaeological wonder featuring the monumental red sandstone Kirti Toran victory arches and Buddhist monasteries.

name: Vadodara
description: Cultural capital of Gujarat home to the majestic 700-acre Laxmi Vilas Palace (4 times size of Buckingham), museums, and Sayaji Baug.

name: Valsad
description: Coastal city renowned for Tithal black sand beach, historic Parnera hilltop fort, Swaminarayan sea temple, and sweet Alphonso mangoes.

name: Amravati
description: Cultural capital of Vidarbha featuring the historic Ambadevi and Ekvira Devi temples and gateway to Melghat Tiger Reserve and Chikhaldara hills.

name: Chhatrapati Sambhaji Nagar
description: Tourism Capital of Maharashtra, gateway to UNESCO World Heritage Ajanta & Ellora cave complexes, Daulatabad Fort, and Bibi Ka Maqbara.

name: Igatpuri
description: Western Ghats hill station enveloped in monsoon mists, home to Vipassana International Academy (Dhamma Giri), Tringalwadi Fort, and waterfalls.

name: Jalgaon
description: Banana City and Golden City of Maharashtra, railhead gateway to the 30 rock-cut Buddhist caves of Ajanta (UNESCO).

name: Kolhapur
description: Historic Maratha kingdom on the Panchganga river famed for Mahalakshmi Ambabai Temple, New Palace museum, wrestling (Kushti), and leather chappals.

name: Mahabaleshwar
description: Highest hill station in the Western Ghats, strawberry capital of India, featuring Arthur's Seat cliff, Venna Lake, and Old Mahabaleshwar temple.

name: Mumbai
description: Financial capital of India featuring UNESCO Victorian Gothic Ensembles, Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus, Elephanta Caves, and Gateway of India.

name: Nagpur
description: Winter Capital of Maharashtra, Orange City, geographic Zero Mile Stone of India, Deekshabhoomi stupa, and tiger gateway to central India.

name: Nashik
description: Wine Capital of India on the Godavari river, host of Kumbh Mela, holding Trimbakeshwar Jyotirlinga, Panchavati, and Pandavleni Buddhist caves.

name: Pune
description: Oxford of the East and Maratha cultural capital, featuring Shaniwar Wada peshwa palace, Sinhagad hilltop fort, Aga Khan Palace, and Osho Ashram.

name: Satara
description: Historic capital of Chhatrapati Shahu Maharaj guarded by Ajinkyatara fort, gateway to UNESCO World Heritage Kaas Valley of Flowers and Thoseghar waterfalls.

name: Amaravati
description: Ancient riverbank Buddhist site boasting the Great Mahachaitya stupa ruins, museums, and seat of Andhra Pradesh administration.

name: Anantapur
description: Rayalaseema historic district home to Gooty Fort, clock tower heritage, and gateway to the hanging pillars of Lepakshi.

name: Chittoor
description: Scenic district renowned for Gurramkonda Fort, Horsley Hills summer sanctuary, and proximity to sacred hill shrines.

name: Guntur
description: Major commercial and historical hub famed for the 14th-century Kondaveedu hilltop fort, Buddhist stupa relics, and chilli trade.

name: Kakinada
description: Deep-water port town nestled along the Bay of Bengal, gateway to Coringa Wildlife Sanctuary second largest mangrove in India.

name: Kurnool
description: Historic city featuring the formidable Konda Reddy Buruju fort, Oravakallu natural rock garden, and Belum Caves.

name: Machilipatnam
description: Ancient Coromandel trading port dating back to Periplus era, world-famous for block-printed Machilipatnam Kalamkari textiles.

name: Nellore
description: Penna riverbank city famed for the ancient Talpagiri Ranganathaswamy temple, Udayagiri fort ruins, and Pulicat lake birds.

name: Rajahmundry
description: Historic city on the sacred Godavari river, birthplace of Telugu literature poet Nannayya, famed for Godavari Arch Bridge.

name: Srikakulam
description: Northern coastal district boasting the 7th-century Arasavalli Sun Temple, Sri Kurmam tortoise shrine, and Kalingapatnam lighthouse.

name: Tirupati
description: World-renowned pilgrimage destination resting at the foothills of the holy Tirumala hills, home to Sri Venkateswara Swamy shrine.

name: Visakhapatnam
description: Cosmopolitan coastal port city with golden beaches, INS Kursura submarine museum, Kailasagiri hill views, and Borra Caves.

name: Vizianagaram
description: Heritage city celebrated for the grand stone-built Vizianagaram Fort, Moti Mahal royal palace, and classical music traditions.

name: Badami
description: Regal capital of the early Chalukyas, renowned for four monolithic rock-cut cave temples carved into red sandstone cliffs above Agastya Lake.

name: Bagalkote
description: Northern Karnataka cultural hub on the Ghataprabha River, gateway to the temple architecture centers of Aihole and Pattadakal (UNESCO).

name: Belagavi
description: Historic border city featuring the massive 12th-century Belgaum Fort with Kamala Basti Jain temple, military heritage, and Gokak Falls.

name: Bengaluru
description: Silicon Valley of India combining modern technology with heritage Lalbagh Botanical Gardens, Tudor-style Bangalore Palace, and Tipu Sultan Summer Palace.

name: Bidar
description: Medieval Bahmani and Barid Shahi capital holding Bidar Fort with 30+ bastions, Mahmud Gawan Madrasa, and fine silver-inlaid Bidriware metalwork.

name: Dharwad
description: Twin cultural capital with Hubli, celebrated as cradle of Hindustani classical music legends (Bhimsen Joshi, Gangubai Hangal) and Dharwad Peda.

name: Gokarna
description: Sacred Arabian coastal town home to the ancient Mahabaleshwar Temple Atmalinga, crescent Om Beach, Kudle Beach, and cliff walking trails.

name: Hampi
description: UNESCO World Heritage monument complex spanning 4,100 hectares of ruins of the medieval Vijayanagara Empire, Stone Chariot, and Virupaksha Temple.

name: Kalaburagi
description: Historical Gulbarga featuring the 14th-century Gulbarga Fort containing the grand roofed Jami Masjid and sacred Sufi shrine of Khwaja Bande Nawaz.

name: Lakkundi
description: Architectural jewel holding 50+ medieval Western Chalukya and Hoysala temples (Brahma Jinalaya, Kasi Visveshwara) and ornate stepped stepwells.

name: Mangalore
description: Coastal port city famed for 10th-century Kadri Manjunatha temple bronze idols, St. Aloysius Chapel frescoes, Panambur beach, and coastal cuisine.

name: Mysuru
description: Cultural Capital of Karnataka home to the Indo-Saracenic Mysore Palace illuminated by 100,000 bulbs, Chamundi Hill, and Mysore Dasara.

name: Somnathpura
description: UNESCO World Heritage site holding the 1268 CE trikuta Chennakeshava Temple, a pinnacle of Hoysala stone relief carving and stellate geometry.

name: Udupi
description: Spiritual destination centered on the 13th-century Sri Krishna Matha founded by Madhvacharya with Kanakana Kindi window, Malpe beach, and St. Mary Island.

name: Vijayapura
description: Historic Adil Shahi capital famed for the colossal dome of Gol Gumbaz (second largest dome in the world) with acoustic Whispering Gallery and Ibrahim Rauza.

name: Alappuzha
description: Venice of the East, heart of Kerala backwaters with houseboats cruising Vembanad Lake, Alappuzha beach lighthouse, and Nehru Trophy Snake Boat Race.

name: Bekal
description: Pristine coastal stronghold famous for the keyhole-shaped 17th-century Bekal Fort rising dramatically out of the Arabian Sea waves.

name: Kannur
description: Land of Looms and Lores, celebrated for vibrant Theyyam ritual dance, Portuguese St. Angelo Fort, and Muzhappilangad drive-in beach.

name: Kasargod
description: Northernmost coastal district holding Ananthapura Lake Temple (only lake temple in Kerala), Chandragiri Fort, and Ranipuram hills.

name: Kochi
description: Queen of the Arabian Sea featuring cantilevered Chinese Fishing Nets, colonial Fort Kochi, Jewish Synagogue, and Mattancherry Dutch Palace.

name: Kollam
description: Ancient spice seaport on Ashtamudi Lake (gateway to backwaters), Tangasseri Lighthouse, and Thangassery British-era church ruins.

name: Kottayam
description: City of Letters and Lakes, rubber plantation belt holding ancient Syrian Christian churches (Valiyapally) and Thazhathangady Juma Masjid.

name: Kovalam
description: World-famous crescent beach destination crowned by the striped red-and-white Vizhinjam Lighthouse, Hawa Beach, and Ayurvedic resorts.

name: Kozhikode
description: Historic City of Spices where Vasco da Gama landed at Kappad in 1498, UNESCO City of Literature, historic beach pier, and culinary delights.

name: Kumarakom
description: Cluster of mangrove islets on Vembanad Lake, home to Kumarakom Bird Sanctuary visited by migratory Siberian cranes, and luxury houseboats.

name: Malappuram
description: Cultural and historical center of Malabar holding Thirunavaya banks of Mamankam medieval festivals and ancient Kottakkal Arya Vaidya Sala.

name: Munnar
description: Verdant hill station in the Western Ghats at 5,200 ft with emerald tea estates, Eravikulam National Park (endangered Nilgiri Tahr), and Anamudi peak.

name: Palakkad
description: Gateway to Kerala across the Palakkad Gap, featuring the granite-built 18th-century Palakkad Fort (Tipu's Fort), Malampuzha Dam, and Kalpathy agraharams.

name: Pathanamthitta
description: Pilgrim capital of Kerala on the Achankovil River, gateway to Sabarimala, Aranmula Parthasarathy Temple with metal mirrors, and Gavi eco-tourism.

name: Sabrimala
description: Sacred forested shrine of Lord Ayyappa perched atop Periyar Tiger Reserve hills, one of the largest annual pilgrimages in the world.

name: Thiruvananthapuram
description: Capital city holding the opulent Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple, Kuthiramalika Palace Museum, Napier Museum, and Kovalam coastline.

name: Thrissur
description: Cultural Capital of Kerala famed for the spectacular Thrissur Pooram festival, circular Vadakkunnathan Temple, and Kerala Kalamandalam.

name: Varkala
description: Unique coastal destination where dramatic red laterite cliffs border the Arabian Sea, 2,000-year-old Janardhana Swamy Temple, and Papanasam beach.

name: Wayanad
description: Mist-clad hill district featuring prehistoric petroglyphs at Edakkal Caves, Chembra Peak heart-shaped lake, Banasura Sagar dam, and spice groves.

name: Kavaratti
description: Capital of Lakshadweep territory, an idyllic coral atoll with crystal-clear turquoise lagoons, marine aquarium, and 17th-century carved wooden Ujra Mosque.

name: Puducherry
description: French Riviera of the East, famed for French Quarter (White Town) colonial architecture, Sri Aurobindo Ashram, Promenade Beach, and experimental township Auroville.

name: Chennai
description: Cultural gateway of South India, featuring Marina Beach, 7th-century Kapaleeshwarar temple, British Fort St. George, and San Thome Basilica.

name: Coimbatore
description: Manchester of South India at the foothills of Nilgiris, home to the colossal Adiyogi Shiva bust statue, Marudhamalai temple, and textile museums.

name: Kanchipuram
description: City of Thousand Temples and world-famous Kanchipuram mulberry silk sarees, holding Ekambareswarar, Kailasanathar, and Varadharaja Perumal temples.

name: Kanniyakumari
description: Southernmost tip of mainland India where Arabian Sea, Indian Ocean and Bay of Bengal converge, with Vivekananda Rock Memorial and Thiruvalluvar Statue.

name: Madurai
description: One of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world, soul of Tamil culture centered on the towering multi-sculptured gopurams of Meenakshi Amman Temple.

name: Mamallapuram
description: UNESCO World Heritage 7th-century Pallava coastal monuments including the Shore Temple, monolithic Pancha Rathas, and Descent of the Ganges rock relief.

name: Ooty
description: Queen of Hill Stations (Udhagamandalam) at 7,350 ft in the Nilgiris, terminus of UNESCO Nilgiri Mountain Toy Train, Botanical Gardens, and tea hills.

name: Rameswaram
description: Sacred Char Dham island temple town connected by Pamban Bridge, home to Ramanathaswamy Temple with world's longest pillared corridor and Dhanushkodi ghost town.

name: Thanjavur
description: Rice Bowl of Tamil Nadu and Chola imperial capital holding UNESCO World Heritage Brihadisvara Temple (Big Temple), Maratha Palace, and Tanjore paintings.

name: Tiruchirappalli
description: Historic Cauvery river city dominated by the dramatic 83-meter high Rockfort Ucchi Pillayar Temple and colossal Ranganathaswamy Temple complex at Srirangam.

name: Bhongir
description: Historic town famed for the monolithic egg-shaped Bhongir Fort built by Western Chalukya ruler Tribhuvanamalla Vikramaditya VI on a single isolated rock.

name: Hyderabad
description: City of Pearls and Nizams, holding the 1591 Charminar, massive Golconda Fort with acoustic engineering, Qutb Shahi Tombs, and Salar Jung Museum.

name: Karimnagar
description: Historic town on the Manair river famed for Silver Filigree (Tarkashi) delicate jewelry, Elgandal hill fortress, and Lower Manair Dam.

name: Khammam
description: Historic town featuring the 10th-century Kakatiya stone Khammam Fort perched on Stambhadri hill, Palair lake, and gateway to Bhadrachalam temple.

name: Warangal
description: Historic Kakatiya capital holding the 12th-century Thousand Pillar Temple, Warangal Fort stone gateways (Kakatiya Kala Thoranam), and UNESCO Ramappa Temple.
